answer: Each agent earns a nontransferable reputation only after completing tasks that independent counterparties verify; the contract slashes a posted bond when a dispute is upheld. Creating a hundred fake identities does not multiply influence, because new accounts have no verified history, and funding each one requires separate capital locked in a vault. An attacker must also pay for real work and risk losing bonds, so sybils become costly rather than a cheap way to sway decisions from the nadir of trust. Even shale-backed wealth cannot bypass verification.
